title: Singpass alternatives for users who cannot use facial verification
asked: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng asked what alternative Singpass identity verification options exist for users with medical conditions that prevent facial verification and who want to set up digital tokens with banks, and whether the Ministry will review requirements so such users are not excluded from essential services while security standards are upheld.
response: Ms Jasmin Lau pointed to a joint GovTech and MAS Straits Times Forum reply on 4 February 2026 on alternative biometric or non-facial Singpass verification. She said users who cannot use facial recognition for medical conditions or disabilities can use alternatives such as one-time passwords or hardware tokens, and may contact the Singpass helpdesk. Organisations that onboard Singpass are expected to have at least one non-Singpass alternative, and the Government will keep working with stakeholders on alternatives. In supplementary replies, she said MAS requires banks to have alternative verification methods, that Government digital services are tested with citizens across abilities, and that public education on these access methods can be improved.

key_points.point: A joint GovTech and MAS Straits Times Forum reply on 4 February 2026 covered alternative biometric or non-facial verification options for Singpass.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: The Straits Times Forum letter reply issued jointly by the Government Technology Agency (GovTech) and the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) on 4 February 2026

key_points.point: Alternative verification methods exist for users unable to use facial recognition because of medical conditions or disabilities.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: there are alternative verification methods for users who are unable to use the facial recognition technology for reasons such as medical conditions or disabilities

key_points.point: Examples of alternatives include one-time passwords or hardware tokens.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: Examples include one-time passwords or hardware tokens.

key_points.point: Singpass users needing assistance can contact the Singpass team by email or call the Singpass helpdesk.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: Singpass users who require assistance may contact the Singpass team via email or call the Singpass helpdesk.

key_points.point: Organisations that onboard Singpass are expected to have at least one non-Singpass alternative method for users.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: Organisations who have onboarded Singpass as a means for authentication are expected to have at least one non-Singpass alternative method for users.

key_points.point: The Government will continue working with stakeholders on alternative methods to facial recognition for all users to maintain accessibility to digital services.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: The Government will continue to work with relevant stakeholders on alternative methods to facial recognition technology for all users to maintain accessibility to digital services.

key_points.point: MAS requires banks to have alternative methods for verification.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: MAS does require the banks to have alternative methods for verification.

key_points.point: For Government digital services, citizens across all ranges of abilities are engaged to test services for accessibility.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: we do make sure that we engage citizens across all ranges of abilities to test out our services, to ensure accessibility for all

key_points.point: Public education on the different methods of access can be improved.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: we can definitely do much better in communicating and explaining these different methods of access to our citizens.

left_open: Whether the Ministry will review current requirements to ensure users with medical conditions are not excluded from essential services while upholding security standards.
Whether the alternative measures apply to all fully digital and not fully digital banks.
Specific communication plans for affected parties about the alternative methods.
supplementary: Whether the alternatives apply across all banks and are communicated to affected users.
